propositions: a parent removed in Jira (peer.parent = None) does not clear the local parent_id due to two independent suppressions: fetcher omits the parent key from snapshot when absent, and inbound_differ refuses to emit parent_id=None

inbound_differ's guard against spurious clears ('avoid accidentally clearing when key is not yet bound') cannot distinguish 'peer has no parent' from 'parent key unresolved', collapsing two states into one None

managed_refs gates the clear but only answers 'rebar set this locally', not 'peer ever had this', leaving a residual window where a locally-set parent on a closed epic (never pushed outbound due to hierarchy gate) was cleared, destroying 63 parent edges in production

inbound clear must gate on positive evidence from peer baseline (ADR-0026 per-binding binding_store record) that the peer once carried this parent, advanced only on observed snapshots to prevent fail-open reads from overwriting good history

three-state parent classification (unobserved key, observed-no-parent, resolved, unresolvable) must be carried from fetcher through differ to emission, with explicit None in snapshot to distinguish 'queried and absent' from 'never queried'

the fix is already live and self-heals into correctness: on first pass after landing no binding has a recorded observation so nothing is cleared; observations accumulate as passes run and feature becomes live per-binding
